title: Homity Pie
subtitle: A deep open tart of potato, leek, and cheddar in a shortcrust case
excerpt: Thick slices of potato and soft leeks bound with cream and sharp cheddar, set in a shortcrust shell. A filling vegetarian supper that holds together cleanly when sliced.
sourceNotes: Based on the Devon wholefoods tradition; this version uses a blind-baked shortcrust case and a generous cheddar top.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The blind-baked case can be made a day ahead and kept covered at room temperature. Fill and bake on the day.

content.text: Homity pie is a baked open tart from the south-west of England, filled with potato, leek, and plenty of cheese. The filling is creamy but not wet, so the pastry stays crisp at the base. Make sure the potatoes are properly cooked through before they go into the case.

Heat the oven to 190C. Roll out the pastry and line a 23cm pie dish. Chill for 20 minutes, then blind bake for 15 minutes with baking beans. Remove the beans and bake for a further 5 minutes. Brush the base with beaten egg and return to the oven for 2 minutes to seal it.
Boil the potato cubes in well-salted water for 8 to 10 minutes until just tender. Drain and leave to steam dry.
Melt the butter in the frying pan over a medium heat. Add the leeks and garlic with a pinch of salt. Cook for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the leeks are soft and just starting to colour.
Tip the drained potatoes into the pan with the leeks. Add the cream, mustard, and half the cheese. Stir gently to combine. Season well with salt and black pepper.
Spoon the filling into the baked pastry case. Level the top and scatter over the remaining cheese.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and golden. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.
Scatter over the chopped parsley if using, and serve directly from the dish.

items.cause: The case was not sealed with egg, or the filling went in too wet.
items.fix: Blind bake fully and brush with egg to seal. Let the filling cool slightly and make sure the potatoes were well drained before mixing.

items.symptom: The filling is loose and won't hold a slice.
items.cause: Too much cream or the potatoes were undercooked.
items.fix: Use only 100ml cream and cook the potatoes until just tender. The filling firms up as it cools, so rest it for 10 minutes before cutting.

items.symptom: The cheese top is browning before the filling is hot.
items.cause: The oven runs hot or the pie dish is too shallow.
items.fix: Cover loosely with foil for the first 15 minutes, then remove to colour the top.
